T: A very particular set of skills. One of them is cooking.
D: A retired agent tracks down the men who kidnapped his daughter in Paris.
P: Serve the mains when Bryan sits down to dinner with Jean-Claude's family.
S: Particular set of skills croque monsieur
built over a very long career

Ham and gruyère between slices of white bread spread with béchamel and Dijon, more béchamel and cheese on top, baked at 200C until bubbling, cut into fingers. Melt 30g butter, stir in 2 tbsp flour, whisk in 300ml milk and cook until thick. Spread 8 slices white bread with Dijon and béchamel, fill with 150g ham and half of 150g gruyère, close and top with the rest of the sauce and cheese. Bake at 200C until bubbling.
Kim's birthday, the karaoke machine and the pony

Vanilla cupcakes with a hidden strawberry jam centre, swirled with pale pink strawberry buttercream and topped with a fresh strawberry and a single candle. Beat 125g butter with 150g caster sugar, add 2 eggs and vanilla, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake 12 in cases at 175C for 18 minutes and cool. Core the middle of each and fill with strawberry jam. Beat 150g soft butter with 300g icing sugar and 4 mashed strawberries until fluffy. Pipe on top and finish each with a strawberry and a candle.
the Albanian gang he hunts down
Filo layered with butter and a filling of feta, ricotta, spinach and egg, rolled into a coil, baked at 190C for 35 minutes until crisp, cut into wedges.
M: the tense family dinner with his old colleague

Chicken roasted with tarragon butter under the skin, with a white wine and Dijon pan sauce, creamy gratin dauphinois and green beans. Slice 1kg potatoes thin, layer with 300ml cream, a crushed garlic clove and salt and bake at 160C for 75 minutes. Mash 60g butter with chopped tarragon and push under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 50 minutes, and rest. Add 150ml white wine and 1 tsp Dijon to the tray, scrape and reduce by half. Steam 300g green beans.
Particular set of skills steak frites
a particular set of skills, put to work in Paris

Entrecôte seared hard and rested, topped with shallot and red wine butter, with thin twice-cooked fries and a sharp Dijon mayo. Reduce 2 chopped shallots in 100ml red wine until almost dry, cool and mash into 80g soft butter with parsley and salt, then chill. Cut 1kg potatoes into thin fries, soak 30 minutes and dry. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes, then 185C until crisp. Sear 4 scotch fillet steaks in a smoking pan to 54C inside and rest 5 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp mayo with 1 tbsp Dijon. Top the steaks with the butter.
W: Caramel poured into ramekins, filled with a custard of eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla, baked in a water bath at 150C for 40 minutes, chilled overnight and turned out.
K: I will find you citron pressé
a glass in Paris before the hunt

Fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup and cold soda water stirred over ice the way Paris cafés serve it, with a splash of cognac for the grown-ups. Squeeze 6 lemons. Fill four tall glasses with ice and add 40ml lemon juice and 20ml sugar syrup to each. Add 30ml cognac to the glasses that want it. Top each with 150ml cold soda water, stir and add a lemon wheel.

w.how: Melt 150g sugar to amber caramel and pour into 4 ramekins. Whisk 4 eggs, 2 yolks, 100g sugar, 500ml milk and the seeds of a vanilla bean. Pour over and bake in a water bath at 150C for 40 minutes. Chill overnight and turn out.
